doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Billie Holiday and the poverty of the Boston gig
summary: At an after-hours joint Billie Holiday sits in with her Chihuahua; the $50-a-week job meant sardines, peanuts and Coke.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: And I listened to that kind of things. And in the meantime I had a gig after hours right across the street there, what was it called, I don’t know but anyway it was a little after- hours joint. We played from maybe two to five in the morning. You know, I mean that type of thing. And one night Billie Holiday walks in. And she sits down on the side there with her little dog, a Chihuahua I think it was. And so put my hand out like this, and the dog grabbed me. She says, “honey don’t do that,” she says, “always do like this.” You know like put your hand out like that. She says, “he won’t bite you then.” She kept her little dog in her purse. And she sang one or two tunes with us that night. Just an informal

thing. It was during the Boston years. And the Boston thing just went on for a while and then my night gig ran out after a year. But I was making $50 a week. And all the other guys says, “well that’s a poor paying club” they says, “the guy didn’t pay you too much money.” But to me—
Was fifty dollars. And I know I ate a lot of sardines and I ate a lot of, what do they call those things, peanuts and Coke. I ate a lot of those.
And I would sleep late in the afternoon so I wouldn’t use up so much energy. That type of thing.
Man, you were paying some dues I guess.
